PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL — PREPARED AT DIRECTION OF OWNER FOR COUNSEL REVIEW
ATTORNEY-CLIENT / WORK-PRODUCT — DO NOT DISTRIBUTE BEYOND INCIDENT COMMAND

# INCIDENT DECISION BRIEF — LOS Ransomware & Unauthorized-Access Matter
Prepared for: Robert Calloway, Owner / Broker
Date: April 28, 2026
Scope: Reconciles the ransomware event (discovered Fri 3/20/2026) with the related
unauthorized-access / data-export findings that bear on the same borrower-notice question.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 0. BOTTOM LINE (read this first)
My reconstruction from the records differs materially from the picture we have been
operating on since the 3/20 evening call. Three corrections:

1. This is not cleanly "an external ransomware attack." A **documented, HIGH-risk
   insider/credential data-exfiltration finding predates the ransomware by ~3 weeks**
   (Interim Security Findings, dated 3/1/2026), and the export pattern appears to have
   **continued after** the credentials were supposedly suspended (Blue Peak, 4/7/2026,
   "weekly exports over the last six weeks"). The ransomware may be the noisy end of a
   longer intrusion, not the whole event.

2. The "restore is expensive, maybe pay" read came from **Raj Anand — who is the named
   subject of the 3/1 finding and remained the sole technical validator gating both the
   restore estimate and the borrower-notice scope.** That is a conflict we cannot leave
   in place. It does not make his estimate wrong; it means it must be independently
   verified before it drives a payment decision.

3. Borrower-notice scope has **broadened, not narrowed.** We now have specific,
   named files implicated across several access vectors, and signals of actual
   PII *export* (not just encryption) — which pushes toward notification obligations,
   not away from them.

Nothing in this brief should be read as a factual conclusion that Mr. Anand did anything
wrong. He has asserted his laptop was stolen and never reported (credential-reuse theory).
Both the "insider" and "compromised-credential" explanations lead to the same next steps:
independent validation and preserve-everything.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. PAY vs. RESTORE — walked back to what the records actually say
(Sources: Raj escalation email 3/20 17:20; Robert→counsel 3/20 19:09; Grace ops note & Raj
"best case restore" note in #general; Interim Findings 3/1; Blue Peak 4/7.)

**Demand:** 2 BTC.

**What the records support about the restore lift:**
- Local backup server: encrypted / unusable (Raj, 3/20).
- Cloud backup: EXISTS, last good point ~72 hours old (~Tuesday PM before Friday discovery).
- Rebuild sequence per Raj (3/25): rebuild infrastructure first, then restore + validate;
  "can't promise LOS integrity until tested."
- Gap to reconstruct: ~3 days (72h) of pipeline activity → manual re-entry; Monday closings
  at risk; pipeline gaps for the ~3 days since last clean snapshot (Grace, 3/20).

**Tradeoffs (not a foregone conclusion):**
- Restore IS feasible. A ~72h-old clean cloud snapshot means the data is substantially
  recoverable without the attacker. Paying a ransom buys decryption speed/completeness —
  it is **not** required to get our data back. That materially weakens the "pay" case on
  recovery grounds.
- The heavy items are real but bounded: environment rebuild + validation + ~3 days of
  re-entry. These are cost/time, not data-loss-forever.
- **Every magnitude estimate here traces to one conflicted source (Raj).** Before payment
  is even evaluated, the restore cost/feasibility should be re-scoped by Blue Peak (or a
  second IR firm) independent of Raj's account and access.
- **Paying likely undercuts the investigation.** A rebuild-and-restore forces the log
  validation most likely to confirm or rule out exfiltration under his credentials.
  Choosing "pay and move on" would forgo that and reduce our own visibility — the opposite
  of what an insider/credential-compromise posture requires.
- **Sanctions/OFAC:** paying certain sanctioned threat actors can be independently unlawful.
  We asked counsel for this read on 3/20 and **have not received it** (see §4). Payment
  should not be evaluated further until that read is in hand.

**My recommendation for the decision:** Default to restore-and-rebuild with independent
IR validation; do not treat payment as live until (a) counsel's sanctions/privilege read
is back and (b) restore feasibility is independently re-scoped. Recovery does not appear to
require payment.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. BORROWER-NOTICE POSTURE — where the plan actually stands
Denise queued a preliminary plan the night of 3/20 (identify files in the affected
environment; determine encrypted vs. accessed/exfiltrated; prep notices; evaluate FinCEN
SAR; document who-knew-what-when). Since then the plan has **fragmented across separate
workstreams and has not been reconciled into one scope.** Current state:

### Confirmed export/exfiltration signals (strongest — points to actual access, not just encryption)
- **Contractor-credential exports (Interim Findings 3/1 + Blue Peak 4/7):**
  four off-hours VPN sessions from a Nashville, TN residential IP (73.214.188.41) on
  2/3, 2/10, 2/17, 2/24; PII/CSV export each session; **38-row bulk pipeline export on 2/24.**
  Named files viewed/exported: **LN-2026-00184 (Mercer), -00211 (Kim), -00237, -00244.**
  Blue Peak (4/7) reports the weekly-export pattern **continued "over the last six weeks."**
  Recommended action already on paper but open: **"determine data destination for exported CSVs."**

### Draft notices ALREADY written and sitting in Drafts (NOT sent — awaiting owner + counsel sign-off)
- Tied to a **former employee accessing files after termination** (Evan Mercer, per #it-support):
  - LN-2025-00002 — James Adams
  - LN-2025-00007 — Chioma Perry
  - LN-2025-00229 — Tiffany Turner
  - **Discrepancy to resolve:** #it-support logged the third post-term file as **LN-2026-00009 (Singh)**,
    but the queued notices/drafts name **LN-2025-00229 (Turner)**. Confirm which before anything sends.

### Working list, notices drafted but HELD pending "Raj's scope confirmation"
- Tied to **compromised UWM wholesale-portal login (Keisha's account, phishing):**
  LN-2026-00522, LN-2026-00008 (Wilson), LN-2026-00010 (Ferguson), LN-2026-00009 (Singh).
  NOTE: gating this on Raj's confirmation is exactly the conflict flagged in §0.

### Identified but NO notices drafted yet (largest un-addressed set)
- **Leo Park access review (report dated 3/31):** ~**34 borrower files** opened over ~2 weeks
  outside ops/admin scope, incl. LN-2026-00554.
- **Marcus Webb:** manual mailbox forwards to a personal address + bulk downloads across
  pipeline sheets and 2 active loan summaries (incl. **LN-2026-00608**); also an undisclosed
  spousal conflict (Danielle Webb, buyer's agent) on 3 files incl. **LN-2026-00211**.

### Overlaps worth noting (suggest these are connected, not separate)
- **LN-2026-00211 (Kim)** appears on BOTH the contractor-export list AND the Marcus conflict list.
- **LN-2026-00009 (Singh)** appears on BOTH the Keisha-portal list AND (per #it-support) the
  post-term list.

**Read on the notice question:** Scope has NOT narrowed. Between the CSV/PII export events,
the 38-row bulk pipeline export, and the six-week weekly pattern, we have affirmative
evidence of NPPI **leaving** the environment for at least some borrowers — not merely
encryption. That posture generally *triggers* notification analysis (GLBA Safeguards /
interagency guidance; NC Identity Theft Protection Act) rather than letting us wait.
The right move is to consolidate ALL vectors into a single deduplicated impacted-borrower
list and let counsel set trigger/timing — not to keep gating on Raj.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. SAR / FinCEN
Flagged as "probably on the table" on 3/20 and never closed out. Ransom demand +
possible customer-info exposure are classic SAR-relevant facts for a financial institution.
No SAR has been filed or formally queued in the records I can see. This is an owner+counsel
decision — surfacing it as still-open, not acting on it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. WHAT COUNSEL STILL OWES US (nothing has come back)
Outside cyber counsel (M. Sloane, Ward Barrett Law) was engaged 3/20. Robert and Denise
both sent requests that evening (payment/sanctions/privilege read; borrower-notice prep).
**There is no responsive email from counsel anywhere in the record.** The following remain
OPEN and should be treated as blockers on the payment decision:
1. OFAC/sanctions analysis on any ransom payment.
2. Privilege posture over the forensic/IR work and internal fact-gathering.
3. Borrower-notification triggers and timing across ALL vectors above (not just the ransomware).
4. FinCEN SAR determination.
5. Whether relying on the finding's subject (Raj) as investigator/validator has created
   any preservation or spoliation exposure, and how to re-structure IR independently.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. RECOMMENDED IMMEDIATE STEPS (for owner decision — none taken unilaterally)
1. Independent IR: have Blue Peak (or a second firm) own restore-feasibility scoping and
   the exfiltration/destination question — remove Raj from the validation path.
2. Freeze the payment question until counsel's sanctions/privilege read is in hand.
3. Consolidate every access vector into ONE deduplicated impacted-borrower list; hold all
   borrower notices for counsel's trigger/timing call; resolve the 00009/00229 discrepancy.
4. Confirm preservation is complete across LOS logs, VPN logs, mailbox traces, and the
   exported-CSV destination.
5. Get the SAR determination from counsel.

Preservation note: this memo and the counsel correspondence are being kept together in the
incident evidence folder (audit/2026-02-supporting-evidence).

Formal incident-record note entered by R. Calloway (Owner) on 2026-04-28. PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL — prepared at direction of owner for counsel review; limit distribution to incident command.

PURPOSE: Reconcile the 3/20/2026 ransomware event with related unauthorized-access findings bearing on borrower notice, and record decision posture.

RECONCILED FINDINGS:
- Insider/credential data-exfiltration finding (Interim Security Findings, 3/1/2026) PREDATES the ransomware by ~3 weeks. Contractor Raj Anand credentials: 4 off-hours VPN sessions from Nashville, TN IP 73.214.188.41 on 2/3, 2/10, 2/17, 2/24; PII/CSV exports each session; 38-row bulk pipeline export 2/24; files not assigned to him (LN-2026-00184, -00211, -00237, -00244). Admin LOS access left provisioned w/o SOW since Nov 2025; Jan IT ticket closed w/o action. Credentials suspended 3/1.
- Blue Peak external review (4/7/2026): weekly-export pattern continued "over the last six weeks," i.e., after the 3/1 suspension. Anand asserts stolen/unreported laptop (credential-reuse theory).
- CONFLICT: the "restore is expensive / consider paying" assessment and the borrower-notice scope gating both ran through Anand, the subject of the 3/1 finding. Independent IR (Blue Peak or 2nd firm) is being moved into the validation role.

PAY vs RESTORE: 2 BTC demand. Local backup encrypted; cloud backup ~72h old and usable, so recovery does not require payment. Restore + rebuild + validation + ~3 days re-entry is the lift. Payment NOT authorized; frozen pending counsel OFAC/sanctions + privilege read (requested 3/20, no response on record).

BORROWER NOTICE: scope broadened, not narrowed. Export evidence indicates NPPI left the environment (not merely encryption). Vectors/files: contractor exports (00184/00211/00237/00244 + six-week pattern); former-employee post-term access (LN-2025-00002 Adams, LN-2025-00007 Perry, and LN-2025-00229 Turner OR LN-2026-00009 Singh — internal records conflict, being resolved); UWM portal compromise (LN-2026-00522, -00008 Wilson, -00010 Ferguson, -00009 Singh); Leo Park review 3/31 (~34 files incl. LN-2026-00554); Marcus Webb mailbox forwards/downloads (incl. LN-2026-00608). Overlaps: LN-2026-00211 and LN-2026-00009 each appear on two lists. Draft notices for the post-term set are written but UNSENT; portal-set notices drafted but held. All held for counsel trigger/timing determination; to be consolidated into one deduplicated impacted-borrower list.

SAR/FinCEN: flagged 3/20 as likely on the table; not filed or formally queued; open for owner+counsel decision.

ACTIONS TAKEN 4/28: (1) Reconciled decision brief saved to incident evidence folder (audit/2026-02-supporting-evidence/Incident_Decision_Brief_2026-04-28_Calloway.md). (2) Privileged email sent to outside cyber counsel (M. Sloane, Ward Barrett Law) requesting views on sanctions, privilege, notification triggers/timing, SAR, and investigator conflict. (3) Leadership status posted to incident command (Calloway/Yamamoto/Holloway). (4) No borrower notices sent, no payment authorized, no SAR filed — all reserved for owner + counsel.

OPEN / BLOCKING ITEMS: counsel OFAC-sanctions read; privilege posture; notice triggers/timing; SAR determination; independent restore-feasibility re-scope and CSV-destination determination; resolve 00009/00229 discrepancy; confirm full preservation (LOS/VPN/mailbox logs + exported-CSV destination).

**The biggest correction: this isn't cleanly "external ransomware," and your restore advisor is conflicted.** Buried in the audit evidence is an internal **Interim Security Findings report dated March 1 — three weeks *before* the March 20 ransomware.** It documents HIGH-risk data exfiltration on **Raj's** contractor credentials: four off-hours VPN sessions from a Nashville, TN residential IP (73.214.188.41) on Feb 3/10/17/24, PII/CSV exports each time, a **38-row bulk pipeline export on 2/24**, against files not assigned to him (LN-2026-00184, -00211, -00237, -00244). His admin LOS access had sat unused-but-live with no SOW since November; a January IT ticket flagging it was closed without action. Credentials were suspended March 1 — yet Blue Peak's **April 7** review says the weekly-export pattern **continued "over the last six weeks,"** i.e., past the suspension. Raj says his laptop was stolen and never reported.

Either way (misuse or stolen credential), the problem is the same: **the "restore is expensive, maybe pay" read and the borrower-notice scope gating both ran through Raj — the subject of that finding.** I'd pull him out of the validation path and put Blue Peak (or a second IR firm) in it.

## Pay vs. restore (walked back to the records, not the call)
2 BTC demand. Local backup encrypted, but a **~72-hour-old clean cloud backup exists** — so recovery does **not** require paying. The real lift is rebuild + validate + ~3 days of re-entry (Monday closings + pipeline gaps). Paying buys speed, not data, and would forgo the log validation most likely to confirm/rule out the exfiltration. I did **not** authorize payment; it should stay frozen until counsel's sanctions read is back.

## Borrower notice — scope *broadened*, not narrowed
The export evidence points to NPPI actually **leaving** the environment, not just being encrypted. ## Legal side — nothing has moved

3. **Short status** posted to the three of you (Calloway/Yamamoto/Holloway) — asked Denise to hold all notice drafts and consolidate vectors into one deduped list.
4. **Formal note logged** in the CRM engagement log for the paper trail.

I did not pay, send borrower notices, or file a SAR — those are decisions I'm leaving with you and counsel. The one thing I'd flag as urgent beyond the memo: chase Sloane, because five weeks in, her read is the gate on both calls.
